brief: A wall-hung spice rack: at least three bins, hung from keyhole hangers.

requirements.evidence: Three hex base cells in a row at q=-1,0,1 (level 0), keyhole hanger on the same face (slot 1) of each, so all backs are flush to one wall plane. Caps close open faces; check_build reports meshClash clear and no issues.
Three 'Bin, full depth, 3 compartments' (hex-bin-full-div3), one per cell, nine compartments in total.
Three hex-acc-keyhole accessories, one per cell. Wall screw spacing and the wall fixing itself are not verified by the configurator.

requirements.requirement: Suitable for food/spices (material safety, moisture resistance)
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit only; food safety and moisture resistance depend on the filament the user chooses.

finish.summary: Built a wall-hung spice rack: three full-depth hex cells in a row, each with a three-compartment bin and a keyhole hanger on the shared back face, closed with caps and joint bolts locked. The fit check is clear. Wall screw positions and food suitability of the material are not verified by the configurator.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
